findings.title: Per-test result for AC-9 and AC-10 is unknown in the results file
quotes: Per-test results are unknown: the suite's runner can't be read per test; the exit code and output are in `suite`.
findings.fix: none needed for the gate if the journey run counts as proof. Otherwise, make the suite runner readable per test, which T-7 now makes possible for self-check suites.

sources.situation: the `tests` array shows `unknown` for both tests. Their pass is shown only by the `journeys` entry, which ran them directly, and by a reused suite exit 0.

findings.note: Delegated: the reused passing suite carries no lines; the journey ran both tests directly and they passed

findings.title: A pytest-style failing entry matches every test of that name in any file
quotes: matches a test only when both its file and its name match (pytest entries have the same form)
else "failed" if any(re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(short)}\b", x) for x in failing)
findings.fix: in the general path, when the entry has `::`, match it with the same `on()` test as the self-check branch (file and name). Keep the name-only match for other entries, as CT-4 says. Add a pytest-style test, or state in CT-4 that the file-and-name rule applies only to self-check.

sources.situation: a suite whose runner is pytest, with `tests/test_a.py::test_one` failing and `tests/test_b.py::test_one` passing. `failing` holds `tests/test_a.py::test_one`. The general path's regex matches the word `test_one` in that entry, so `tests/test_b.py` `test_one` is recorded `failed`. CT-4 says a `<file>::<name>` entry must match on both file and name, and it says pytest entries have this form.

a pytest suite fails `FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_one`. A spec test `tests/test_b.py::test_one` is then marked `failed` by the `\b{short}\b` search over `failing`, or it is run alone. Only the self-check branch got the file-and-name `on()` match.

findings.reason: CT-4 says a `<file>::<name>` entry, pytest included, matches on both file and name. Only the self-check branch applies `on()` (evidence.py:437-439). The general branch (evidence.py:444) uses `\b{short}\b` over `failing`, so `tests/test_a.py::test_one` also marks `tests/test_b.py` `test_one` as `failed`.
findings.where: src/nio/evidence.py, collect, the general-path `result` expression (diff line 36)

findings.title: `crashed` is set by a self-check file's `ran 0 tests` line
quotes: `crashed` is not set by one file's `ran 0 tests` line in a self-check suite: results are read per test.
crashed = bool(implement.wrong_reason(name, 0 if code_ok else 1, suite["output"])) or
findings.fix: in the `crashed` expression, leave out the `wrong_reason` term when `sc` is True, as the `not sc` guard already does for the other term.

sources.situation: one self-check file runs no test because its name filter matched nothing (FR-1), so it prints `ran 0 tests, 0 failed`. `wrong_reason` returns "no tests ran", so `crashed` is True for the whole suite. The self-check branch never reads `crashed`, so today's results are the same. The flag still breaks the written rule, and it would mislead the general path if that path ever handled a self-check run.

findings.note: Delegated: the self-check branch never reads crashed; no result changes

findings.title: Reused epic-close suite runs give `unknown` per test, not the per-test results of FR-8
quotes: WHEN jury evidence reads a suite run whose output has self-check lines
reused: the review of T-7 ran this suite at 0dd6e049 and it exited 0
findings.fix: either keep the self-check lines of a passing review run with the reuse record, or state in FR-8 or D-261106-grjt that reused runs give `unknown` per test.

sources.situation: the epic's configured suite is a self-check suite. Its epic-close review run passed, so evidence reuses that run, and the reused output is the one-line note above. Neither the runner nor the self-check branch can read it, so each test is `unknown`. The per-test results that US-3 asks for do not appear on this common path, and the spec neither says so nor handles it.

findings.note: Delegated: reuse happens only on a passing suite (D-261106-grjt); the #88 case is a failing suite, which runs fresh and is read per test. Follow-up noted in the PR

findings.title: Pytest failing entries still match by name only
quotes: A failing-test entry of the form `<file>::<name>` matches a test only when both its file and its name match (pytest entries have the same form)
findings.fix: apply `on()` to the generic branch for any `failing` entry that contains `::`, and keep the name-only match for entries without it. Add a pytest-form test with the same name in two files.

sources.situation: a pytest suite fails `FAILED tests/test_a.py::test_one`. A spec test `tests/test_b.py::test_one` is then marked `failed` by the `\b{short}\b` search over `failing`, or it is run alone. Only the self-check branch got the file-and-name `on()` match.

findings.title: Self-check file match breaks when the runner's cwd differs from the repo root
findings.fix: compare path suffixes (`file.endswith(path)` or the reverse) on whole segments, not a substring.

sources.situation: the `ok` and `FAIL` lines carry a path relative to the suite's cwd, but `on()` tests `file in <path>` with the spec's repo-relative `file`. If the suite does `cd tests && python test_a.py`, the printed path is `test_a.py`, and `tests/test_a.py` is not contained in it. Every test then reads `failed` when the suite exits non-zero, or `didn't run` when it exits 0. In the opposite direction, the substring test also lets `test_a.py` match `tests/sub/test_a.py`.

findings.note: Delegated: suites here run from the repo root; T-10 makes the file match compare whole paths
